drafted_from: workflow:method-find-the-constraints's row in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json (its job, input schema and the step named in the worked example)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:method-find-the-constraints on: decide the price of a five-lesson online bread-baking course for home bakers."
no_lists_because: It is a way of thinking a request through, answered in words step by step, and it reads and writes no list.
instructions: 1. Write the decision in one plain sentence, for example "decide the price of a five-lesson online bread-baking course for home bakers", and say "Run workflow:method-find-the-constraints" with it as request (at least 10 characters).

2. The AI starts it with tool:start-a-recipe-run (row workflow:method-find-the-constraints) and answers its steps in order: outcome, question, baseline, rule-out, owner, smallest-change, automate, risk, production, proof; each answer is refused until every check of the step is answered about this request.

3. At rule-out, write the table of extremes (people, use, money, memory, disk, setup, time, absence, failure) and count how many options survive; if more than a few survive, name the constraint you are missing.
4. Read what the last step, proof, hands back: how success and failure will be checked and the date it will be checked.

worked_examples.title: Name what a course price is chosen to maximize
worked_examples.ask: Run workflow:method-find-the-constraints: decide the price of a five-lesson online bread-baking course for home bakers.

input.request: Decide the price of a five-lesson online bread-baking course for home bakers

worked_examples.given: Read from tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json, step outcome: its submit shape is answer (at least 40 characters) and checks, which holds one check, outcome-price-names-what-it-optimizes (at least 20 characters). The request is the one in the input above.
